curated_by: Owner-approved curation, drafted by Claude (Claude Code) from general knowledge; citations not checked against the books. Owner review pending.
note: Curated, sourced readings (not AI). Options are equal and unranked.

options.label: Moses wrote it, as tradition holds
options.detail: The long-standing Jewish and Christian view: Moses wrote the five books, apart from small later notes such as his death. Gleason Archer defends it. Owner review pending.

options.label: Moses used earlier sources; later editors added to it
options.detail: Duane Garrett argues that Moses drew on older sources and that the books were edited after him. Owner review pending.

options.label: Four written sources combined over time
options.detail: The documentary hypothesis, classically stated by Julius Wellhausen: separate documents (J, E, D, P) were joined by editors. Owner review pending.

options.label: Separate sources, joined once by a compiler
options.detail: Joel Baden’s renewed form of the documentary hypothesis: independent sources were combined by a single compiler. Owner review pending.

options.label: A core text, expanded in stages
options.detail: The supplementary view, argued by John Van Seters: later writers extended an earlier work. Owner review pending.

options.label: Independent blocks of tradition, joined late
options.detail: Rolf Rendtorff argues that larger units (such as the ancestors and the exodus) grew separately before being joined. Owner review pending.

statements.label: What the text says: Genesis does not name its writer
statements.detail: Genesis itself does not say who wrote it.

statements.label: What the text says: Moses wrote some parts
statements.detail: Exodus says that Moses wrote down certain things, such as the LORD’s words at Sinai (Exodus 24:4). It does not say who wrote the whole book.

statements.label: What the text says: Leviticus does not name its writer
statements.detail: Leviticus reports words the LORD spoke to Moses. It does not say who wrote the book.

statements.label: What the text says: Moses wrote some parts
statements.detail: Numbers says that Moses wrote down the stages of the journey (Numbers 33:2). It does not say who wrote the whole book.

statements.label: What the text says: Moses wrote “this law”
statements.detail: Deuteronomy says that Moses wrote “this law” (Deuteronomy 31:9). The book also reports Moses’ death (Deuteronomy 34).
